title: Kita is now SOC 2® Type II compliant
summary: Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant. The standards the attestation was performed under, its scope, its relevance to third-party risk management for regulated lenders, and how to obtain the report.
body_markdown:
Kita is SOC 2® Type II compliant. An independent CPA firm has examined the controls supporting the Kita platform and issued our SOC 2 Type II report on the organization’s controls relevant to security.


ReportSOC 2 Type II


StandardAICPA SSAE 18, 2017 Trust Services Criteria


Period of performance18 May to 18 August 2026


Report issued12 October 2026


ControlsRelevant to security


## SOC 2 Type II overview


System and Organization Controls (SOC) reports are internal control reports defined by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). They examine the services a service organization provides so that its customers can assess and address the risk of an outsourced service.


Kita’s SOC 2 Type II attestation was performed under:


- SSAE No. 18, Attestation Standards: Clarification and Recodification, including AT-C section 105, Concepts Common to All Attestation Engagements, and AT-C section 205, Assertion-Based Examination Engagements (AICPA, Professional Standards).
- SOC 2 Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, or Privacy (AICPA Guide).
- TSP section 100, 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy.


The examination was conducted by an independent, licensed CPA firm. The resulting report describes the Kita system, assesses whether that description is fairly presented, and evaluates whether Kita’s controls were suitably designed and operated effectively over the period of performance.


## Scope


The report covers the controls supporting the Kita platform, the system through which customers submit borrower documents and receive structured data and credit assessments. The system description and the complete list of in-scope services are set out in the report.


## Relevance for regulated lenders


Banks, credit unions, CDFIs and other regulated lenders remain responsible for managing the risk of the third parties they rely on. US banking agencies’ Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management (June 2023) expects institutions to assess a provider’s information security and to review independent reviews such as SOC reports during due diligence and ongoing monitoring.


The Kita SOC 2 Type II report is intended to support that review. Lenders should read it alongside the complementary user entity controls it lists, which describe the controls that remain the customer’s responsibility.


Kita returns credit assessments. Lending decisions remain with the lender, and a SOC 2 report does not attest to the outcome of any individual assessment.


## Relationship to ISO 27001


Kita is also[ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified](https://www.kita.ai/blog/iso-27001-certified) . ISO 27001 certifies the information security management system. The SOC 2 Type II report attests to the operating effectiveness of specific controls over a defined period. The two are complementary.


## Obtaining the report


The SOC 2 Type II report is available to customers and prospective customers under NDA. Emailsupport@kita.ai . Additional documentation is available on the[Kita Trust Center](https://trust.kita.ai/) and the[security page](https://www.kita.ai/security) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How often is the Kita SOC 2® Type II report issued?


Kita commissions a SOC 2 Type II examination annually. The current report covers the period 18 May 2026 to 18 August 2026 and was issued on 12 October 2026.


### Which Trust Services Criteria does the report address?


The report is issued under the 2017 Trust Services Criteria and addresses the Security criteria (the common criteria), which apply to every SOC 2 examination. Request the report for the full scope.


### How do I obtain the report?


Email support@kita.ai. In line with standard practice for SOC 2 reports, it is provided to customers and prospective customers under a non-disclosure agreement.


### Where are user entity responsibilities described?


Complementary user entity controls, the responsibilities that remain with the customer, are listed in the report. Your security team should review them as part of vendor due diligence.


### Is SOC 2 a certification?


No. SOC 2 is an attestation report issued by an independent CPA firm under AICPA attestation standards. Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant and separately ISO 27001 certified.
